9. In Writ Petition No. 742 of 2012 the petitioner Jiangsu Lingzhi Environmental Protection Co. Ltd (JLEPCL) challenged the legality and propriety of the order of Review Panel dated 5-10-2011 narrating the facts as mentioned above and further stated that the review panel-2 passed the impugned order beyond its jurisdiction as contemplated under Rule 60(3)(ka) to (Cha) of the Public Procurement Rules, 2008 and the review committee can only given suggestion for taking necessary steps. The complaint as made by the WABAG Ltd. was barred by limitation as per provision of Article 57 of Schedule 2 of the PPR. The bank guarantee as submitted by way of swift massage is genuine one ad the TEC found the same valid. The order of the Review Panel has not been made in accordance with law so the same is declared to have been made without lawful authority. 

 11. In Writ Petition No. 10380 of 2011 Mr Mahbub Shafique, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioner submits that the Government after passing the order dated 5-10-2011 by the 'Review Panel-2 has not been challenged the same so it is the duty of the Government to implement the' decision of the review panel. As the provision of Rule 60(5) the decision of the Review Panel will be final and the parties concerned will take steps as per decision of the Review Panel so it is the duty of the respondents to implement the decision of the Review' Panel. He submits that as per provision of Rule 22(2) of the PPR the bank guarantee must be submitted with the tender document in a particular form' and the same should be enforceable hi Bangladesh through a associated international reputed Bank. In the instant case the Islami Bank categorically denied to make the bank guarantee issued by the Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, Nanjing Branch, China enforceable in Bangladesh. He submits that the instant complaint was not barred by limitation, in view of the fact that when the VA Tech WABAG Ltd. apprehended that they may be prejudiced in not taking action by the authority in accordance with the terms of the PPR. They filed complain within seven days before the authority concerned so the said complaint was well within time, The review Panel elaborately consider all the issues and came to the conclusion that the bank guarantee as submitted by way of swift message is not enforceable in Bangladesh.' So the offer as made by JLEPC1-DCL-VJ was declared to be non-responsive one. There is no option on behalf of 'the respondents to implement the decision of the Review Panel. 

 12. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney-General appeared on behalf of respondent No. 1 in the Writ Petition No. 10380 of 2011 and submits that the bank guarantee as submitted by the JLEPCI-DCL-JV is a valid bank guarantee and the same has been found satisfactory after holding inquiry as per provision of Rule 24 of the PPR. He submits that Rule 22 should be read with Rule 24 of the PPR. The procuring entity rightly declared JLEPC1-DCL-JV responsive. He summits that the law complaint so the complaint has filed by WABAG Ltd; was not at all maintainable. He submitted that Tech WABAG Ltd. in writing admitted in different application that they had knowledge about the bank guarantee of JLEPC1-DCHV Ltd. Sent through swift message long before filed within 7 days from the date of knowledge so the instant complaint was barred by limitation. He submits that the satisfaction as to the genuineness of the bank guarantee is of the procuring entity and after holding inquiry the Government found that the bank guarantee issued by Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Ltd and sent through swift message is genuine one. He submits that the object of submission on such bank guarantee is only to resist the frivolous offer and the offer made by the JLEPCI-DCL-J Ltd. was not frivolous one. According to him the procurement of Rule 22 (2) of PPR has been complied with. 

 13. Mr. Anisul Haque, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioner in Writ petition No. 742 of 2012 submits that the order of the Review Panel acted beyond its jurisdiction as contemplated under Rule 60(6) of the PPR. The Review Panel can given suggestion. But in the instant case the Review Panel held that the bank guarantee submitted by the JLEPCI(DCL(JV is not acceptable and declared it's offer non responsive. He submits that the complaint filed by the VA Tech Wabag Ltd. is barred by limitation as per provision of Article 57 Schedule-2 of the PPR. The Review Panel could not settle the issue of limitation in view of special limitation proved in schedule 2 of the PPR. He submits that the provision of Rule 22(2) of PPR has been provided to resist the frivolous tender and TEC itself after holding inquiry found that the bank guarantee as submitted by JLEPCI-DCL-JV is valid bank guarantee. It is the satisfaction of the TEC whether the offer as made by the JLEPCI.DCL-JV is frivolous or not. There was no illegality in the decision of the TEC. 

 21. In Writ Petition No. 742 of 2012 the JLEPCL challenged the said order of the Review Panel, firstly on the ground that the complaint as lodged by the WABAG Ltd. was barred by the limitation. In view of the specific ground that the complaint was barred by limitation, let as considered the said ground first. Rule 57 of the PPR provided the provision to lodge the complaint which runs as follows:— 

 In the instance the tender process the Project Director is the relevant officer before whom the formal complaint should be lodged. The limitation as provided in the scheduled 2 of PPR is a follows:— 

 27. On perusal of the documents Annexure-G to the Writ Petition No. 10380 of 2011 it appears to us that the petitioner had know-ledge about the above defect of JLEPCL-DCLJV before 14-8-2011. Wherein they did not say anything regarding their date of knowledge. It appears from the impugned order i.e. the order of the Review Panel-2 that the Review Panel in Appeal framed three issues. Out of which issue No.2 was about the limitation Review Panel answered the said issue in the following manner:— 

 29. Since the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 10380 of 2011 admitted in the Annexure-1 that during the opening of the offers the other bidder JLEPCL-DCLJA has been identified to have submitted swift copy of Bank Guarantee from Shanghi Pudong Development Bank, Nanjing Branch, China and advised through Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd. Kawran Bazar Branch, Dhaka Ref No. 001 dated 29-6-2011 'without any risk responsibility and engagement on our part" and in the formal complaint Annexure-1 as lodged by the VA Tech Wabag Ltd. mentioned the said fact and did not disclose anything so far their alleged date of knowledge is concerned, we have no hesitating to hold that the statement made on 29-8-2011 before the Chairman, BSCIC regarding dated knowledge is a creation of "after thought" only to get escape from limitation. 

 30. Accordingly, we are of the view that the complaint lodged by the petitioner VA Tech WABAG Ltd. under Rule 57 read with schedule 2 of the PPR was barred by limitation and the Project Direction rightly held so.
